blogs.title: Direct Preference Optimization in Plain English: Aligning LLMs Without Reinforcement Learning
blogs.description: A high-level explainer of DPO for non-specialists. Covers why RLHF is complex, how DPO replaces it with a simple classification-style loss, what the beta parameter does, and why DPO tends to be more stable and lighter on compute while still matching or beating PPO-based RLHF.

blogs.title: Your Language Model Is Secretly a Reward Model: The Intuition Behind DPO
blogs.description: Unpacks the paper’s core idea: reparameterizing rewards as a ratio of policy probabilities to a reference policy. Explains the Bradley–Terry preference model, why the partition function cancels, how preference data becomes a direct policy objective, and what it means that many reward functions are equivalent up to a constant.

blogs.title: From PPO to DPO: What You Gain, What You Lose
blogs.description: A pragmatic comparison between traditional RLHF with PPO and DPO. Discusses training stability, hyperparameter sensitivity, compute costs, reward–KL trade-offs, and when PPO may still be preferable (e.g., long-horizon exploration), using the paper’s reward/KL frontier results and temperature robustness findings.

blogs.title: Hands-On DPO: A Practical Guide to Training From Preferences With One Loss
blogs.description: Step-by-step instructions for running DPO: choosing a reference model, preparing preference pairs, setting beta, and optimizing the DPO loss. Includes tips for reusing public preference datasets, initializing the reference when no SFT model is available, and avoiding degeneration with the per-example weighting.

blogs.title: How DPO Was Tested: Sentiment Control, Summarization, and Dialogue
blogs.description: Summarizes the experiments and key takeaways: DPO’s superior reward–KL frontier in sentiment control, higher win rates than PPO in summarization, competitive or better performance than Best-of-N in dialogue, GPT-4 vs human evaluation agreement, and initial evidence of out-of-distribution generalization to CNN/DailyMail.

blogs.title: The Math Behind the Magic: Why the DPO Objective Works
blogs.description: A gentle dive into the theory: the KL-constrained optimal policy form, the change-of-variables that ties policies to rewards, equivalence classes of reward functions, and why DPO avoids value baselines that can destabilize actor–critic methods. Connects DPO to control-as-inference and clarifies the role of the reference policy.

blogs.title: What DPO Means for AI Alignment and Product Teams
blogs.description: Explores the broader implications: faster, cheaper alignment cycles; simpler pipelines; easier scaling of preference learning; and better controllability for real-world applications. Also covers limitations and open questions, including OOD behavior, multi-attribute trade-offs, evaluation prompt sensitivity, and scaling to much larger models.
